tasks.title: Echo server
tasks.statement:
Write a handler for GET /ws: after the upgrade it reads text messages and answers each with «echo: TEXT» (the word «echo», a colon, a space and the received text). When the client closes, the handler ends. main (provided) connects a client, sends two messages and prints the replies.

Expected output:
Some("echo: hello")
Some("echo: how are you")
tasks.hint: upgrade.on_upgrade(handle); while let Some(Ok(msg)) = socket.recv().await { if let Message::Text(t) = msg { socket.send(Message::Text(format!(..).into())) } }

tasks.title: Handshake: 101 and refusal
tasks.statement:
The route GET /ws performs the upgrade (an empty on_upgrade handler that does nothing is enough), and GET /plain answers with the plain text «not a socket». main connects to /ws and prints the handshake status, then tries to connect to /plain and prints whether that succeeded (it does not: the handshake is not 101). Write only the router and the handlers.

Expected output:
«101 Switching Protocols
connected to /plain: false»
tasks.hint: The Response comes from on_upgrade; /plain is an async fn returning &'static str.

tasks.title: Closing on command
tasks.statement:
GET /ws: reads messages; on receiving the text «bye» it replies «goodbye» and closes the socket (socket.close()). Any other text is answered with «ok». The client in main sends «hello», «bye» and then tries to read one more message; after the server closes, it gets None.

Expected output:
Some("ok")
Some("goodbye")
None
tasks.hint: if t.as_str() == "bye" { send; socket.close().await; break; }

tasks.title: Binary frames
tasks.statement:
GET /ws: a text message is returned in upper case, and a binary one with its bytes in reverse order. The client in main sends «abc», the binary [1, 2, 3, 4] and then «xyz», and prints all three replies.

Expected output:
«text ABC
binary [4, 3, 2, 1]
text XYZ»
tasks.hint: Message::Binary(bytes): bytes is Bytes; to_vec(); reverse(); Message::Binary(v.into()).

tasks.title: The server checks liveness
tasks.statement:
GET /ws: right after the upgrade the server sends a Ping with the data «hi», waits for a Pong (the client library answers a Ping by itself while it is reading the socket) and, once it gets a Pong with the same data, sends the text «pong received». main reads the client's messages until a text arrives and prints it.

Expected output:
Some("pong received")
tasks.hint: socket.send(Message::Ping("hi".into())); then recv() until Message::Pong(data).

tasks.title: split: reading and writing in different tasks
tasks.statement:
GET /ws: after the upgrade, split the socket (socket.split()). The reading task receives text and turns it into upper case, sending it into an mpsc queue; the writing task takes from the queue and writes to the socket. Replies must come in the same order. The client in main sends five messages in a row and prints five replies.

Expected output:
Some("ONE")
Some("TWO")
Some("THREE")
Some("FOUR")
Some("FIVE")
tasks.hint: let (mut tx, mut rx) = socket.split(); tokio::spawn for the writer; the reader runs in the function itself; mpsc::channel(16).

tasks.title: Shared chat: to everyone connected
tasks.statement:
The application state is a broadcast::Sender<String>. GET /ws: every text message received from a client is broadcast to everyone connected (the sender included); each client gets the broadcast through its own receiver (subscribe). The writing and reading parts are separate tasks. main connects two clients, sends a message from the first and prints what both received.

Expected output:
a: Some("hello all")
b: Some("hello all")
tasks.hint: Set up the subscription (tx.subscribe()) before you start reading from the client; select! between the channel's recv() and the socket's next().

tasks.title: Hub: subscribing and publishing per room
tasks.hint: entry(room).or_insert_with(|| broadcast::channel(16).0).subscribe(); publish: clone the Sender under the read lock, send after releasing it.

tasks.title: Cleaning up emptied rooms
tasks.statement:
Add to the Hub from the previous task gc(&self) -> usize, which removes rooms that have no receivers at all (Sender::receiver_count() == 0) and returns the number removed, and rooms_count(&self) -> usize. Check that after unsubscribing (dropping the receivers) gc removes the empty rooms but leaves the occupied ones alone.

Expected output:
«3
gc: 0
gc: 2 left 1
gc: 0 left 1
gc: 1 left 0
gc: 0»
tasks.hint: map.retain(|_, tx| tx.receiver_count() > 0); the number removed is the difference of the sizes.

tasks.title: Parsing protocol commands
tasks.statement:
The client sends JSON commands: {"type":"subscribe","room":N}, {"type":"send","room":N,"text":..}, {"type":"typing","room":N}. Define an enum Command (serde, tag = "type", snake_case) and a function parse(text: &str) -> Result<Command, String>, where the error is a ready-made JSON event {"type":"error","message":..}: «not JSON» for a syntax error, «unknown command» for an unknown type or wrong fields, «too long» for send with text longer than 20 characters (chars), and «empty text» for text that is empty after trim. Everything else is Ok.

Expected output:
«Ok(Subscribe { room: 3 })
Ok(Send { room: 3, text: "hello" })
Ok(Typing { room: 1 })
Err("{\"message\":\"not JSON\",\"type\":\"error\"}")
Err("{\"message\":\"unknown command\",\"type\":\"error\"}")
Err("{\"message\":\"unknown command\",\"type\":\"error\"}")
Err("{\"message\":\"too long\",\"type\":\"error\"}")
Err("{\"message\":\"empty text\",\"type\":\"error\"}")
Err("{\"message\":\"unknown command\",\"type\":\"error\"}")»
tasks.hint: serde_json::from_str::<Command>; tell e.is_syntax() and e.is_data() apart.

tasks.title: Server event format
tasks.hint: #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "snake_case")].

tasks.title: Rooms over a socket
tasks.statement:
The state is a Hub (the starter has Arc<Mutex<HashMap<i64, broadcast::Sender<String>>>>, with the method room(id) -> Sender already written). GET /ws: the protocol is as follows: the text «sub N» subscribes the connection to room N (reply «ok N»), the text «say N TEXT» publishes the text to room N (subscribers get «[N] TEXT»). A subscriber gets events only from its own rooms. To forward events from the channels into the socket, use a task per connection (an mpsc queue of outgoing messages). Client A is subscribed to 1, B to 1 and 2, C to 2; messages are published to rooms 1 and 2.

Expected output:
Some("ok 1") Some("ok 1") Some("ok 2") Some("ok 2")
A: Some("[1] hello first")
B: [Some("[1] hello first"), Some("[2] hello second")]
C: Some("[2] hello second")
tasks.hint: For each subscription, spawn a task that reads the broadcast::Receiver and puts strings into an mpsc::Sender<String>; the writing half of the socket reads from the mpsc.

tasks.title: Token before the upgrade
tasks.statement:
GET /ws?token=T: the tokens «t-anna» → anna and «t-boris» → boris (a simple table in the handler). A wrong or missing token gets a 401 response BEFORE the upgrade (the client's connection ends with an Http error with status 401). A valid one gets the upgrade and the server's first message: «hello, NAME» (the word «hello», a comma, a space and the user's name). main connects in three variants.

Expected output:
«/ws?token=t-anna: Some("hello, anna")
/ws?token=bad: denied 401
/ws: denied 401
/ws?token=t-boris: Some("hello, boris")»
tasks.hint: Query<Q> with an Option<String>; return (StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED, ..).into_response() instead of on_upgrade.

tasks.title: Membership on subscribe
tasks.statement:
The starter keeps membership in memory: anna is in rooms 1 and 2, boris only in 2. GET /ws?user=NAME (we skip token checking): the text «sub N» is answered with «ok N» if the user is a member of room N, and with the JSON error {"type":"error","message":"no access"} if not (including for rooms that do not exist at all: they are indistinguishable). Any other text is ignored. Check anna and boris.

Expected output:
«anna 1: Some("ok 1")
anna 2: Some("ok 2")
anna 3: Some("{\"type\":\"error\",\"message\":\"no access\"}")
boris 1: Some("{\"type\":\"error\",\"message\":\"no access\"}")
boris 2: Some("ok 2")
boris 3: Some("{\"type\":\"error\",\"message\":\"no access\"}")»
tasks.hint: A table: fn members(room: i64) -> &'static [&'static str]; compare with the name.

tasks.title: The author comes from the session
tasks.statement:
GET /ws?user=NAME (the name comes from the "session" and is considered verified). The client sends JSON {"text":..,"author":..}; the client's author field is IGNORED (it may be somebody else's). The server replies with JSON {"author":NAME_FROM_SESSION,"text":..}. Invalid JSON gets {"error":"not JSON"}. Check an attempt to forge the author.

Expected output:
«Some("{\"author\":\"anna\",\"text\":\"hello\"}")
Some("{\"error\":\"not JSON\"}")
Some("{\"author\":\"anna\",\"text\":\"more\"}")»
tasks.hint: A struct In { text: String } without an author field (serde skips unknown fields by default).

tasks.title: A lagging receiver
tasks.statement:
Create a broadcast channel with capacity 2, a subscriber rx, and send 5 events (1…5) without reading anything. Then read rx.recv() in a loop: print the first Lagged(n) error (how many were skipped), and then the remaining values until the channel is empty (try_recv returns Empty). After that, send one more event and make sure it arrives without errors. Define a function next_event(&mut Receiver<i32>) -> String that turns the result of a read into «event N» or «resync (skipped K)».

Expected output:
«resync (skipped 3)
event 4
event 5
true
event 6
channel closed»
tasks.hint: match rx.recv().await { Ok(v) => .., Err(RecvError::Lagged(k)) => .., Err(RecvError::Closed) => .. }

tasks.title: A bounded outgoing queue
tasks.statement:
The function push(tx: &mpsc::Sender<String>, msg: String) -> Push must put a message into the client's queue without blocking (try_send) and return Push::Queued, Push::Slow (the queue is full: the client must be disconnected) or Push::Gone (the receiver is already closed). With a queue of capacity 3: print the result of five sends without reading, then read one message and one more send succeeds; then close the receiver.

Expected output:
1: Queued
2: Queued
3: Queued
4: Slow
5: Slow
Some("m1")
Queued
Gone
tasks.hint: TrySendError::Full / TrySendError::Closed.

tasks.title: Closing silent clients
tasks.statement:
GET /ws: if no frame has come from the client (text, binary or Pong) for more than 150 ms, the server closes the connection (after the close, the client's read returns None). Every client message resets the timer. main: client 1 sends messages every 60 ms four times (getting «ok» for each) and stays alive; client 2 stays silent and must be closed.

Expected output:
«active: Some("ok")
active: Some("ok")
active: Some("ok")
active: Some("ok")
silent closed: true»
tasks.hint: tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_millis(150), socket.recv()) in a loop; Err(_) means timeout → break.

tasks.title: Ping on a timer
tasks.statement:
GET /ws: every 50 ms the server sends a Ping (the first one right after the upgrade) and stops after 3 pings, then sends the text «pings: 3» and waits for the client to close the connection (read socket.recv() to the end); otherwise the connection would be torn down with a reset while the client is still answering pings. The client in main counts Pings until the text arrives; that is already in the provided main.

Expected output:
«pings received 3, text "pings: 3"»
tasks.hint: tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_millis(50)); the first tick fires immediately.

tasks.title: Presence by connection count
tasks.statement:
Implement Presence: connect(&mut self, user: &str) -> bool (true if the user has just come online, i.e. had 0 connections), disconnect(&mut self, user: &str) -> bool (true if they went offline, i.e. no connections are left; a spare disconnect for an unknown user returns false and breaks nothing), is_online(&self, user: &str) -> bool, and online(&self) -> Vec<String> in alphabetical order.

Expected output:
true
false
true
["anna", "boris"]
false
true true
true
false
false
["boris"]
tasks.hint: HashMap<String, usize>; remove the entry when it reaches zero.

tasks.title: Cleanup on any ending
tasks.statement:
The state holds a log Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>>. GET /ws?user=NAME: on connect the log gets «joined NAME», and when the connection ends in ANY way (clean close, drop, error), «left NAME». Implement this with a guard struct with Drop, living in the connection handler. main connects a client, then abruptly destroys it (drop without Close) and prints the log after 200 ms.

Expected output:
["joined anna"]
["joined anna", "left anna"]
tasks.hint: struct Cleanup { user: String, log: Arc<Mutex<Vec<String>>> } impl Drop { fn drop(&mut self) { push("left ..") } } is created at the start of handle.

tasks.title: The leave event
tasks.statement:
A shared chat on a broadcast::Sender<String>. GET /ws?user=NAME: on connect, the JSON {"type":"join","user":NAME} is broadcast to everyone (the new user included), and on disconnect, {"type":"leave","user":NAME}. A client gets events through its own receiver. main connects anna, then boris; anna reads their joins; boris closes cleanly, and anna gets the leave of boris. Print what anna sees.

Expected output:
«anna sees: Some("{\"type\":\"join\",\"user\":\"anna\"}")
anna sees: Some("{\"type\":\"join\",\"user\":\"boris\"}")
boris sees: Some("{\"type\":\"join\",\"user\":\"boris\"}")
anna sees: Some("{\"type\":\"leave\",\"user\":\"boris\"}")»
tasks.hint: Set up the broadcast subscription BEFORE broadcasting join; send leave from a Drop guard or after the read loop.

tasks.title: "Typing..." not to yourself
tasks.statement:
A shared chat: events are broadcast in a broadcast::Sender<(u32, String)> (connection id, JSON). GET /ws: each connection is given a number (an AtomicU32 counter starting at 1). A client sends the text «typing»; the others get {"type":"typing","conn":N}, but not the sender; all other texts are broadcast to everyone, the sender included, as {"type":"say","conn":N,"text":..}. Three clients: the second types, then the first speaks.

Expected output:
«a: Some("{\"conn\":2,\"type\":\"typing\"}")
c: Some("{\"conn\":2,\"type\":\"typing\"}")
a: Some("{\"conn\":1,\"text\":\"hello\",\"type\":\"say\"}")
b: Some("{\"conn\":1,\"text\":\"hello\",\"type\":\"say\"}")
c: Some("{\"conn\":1,\"text\":\"hello\",\"type\":\"say\"}")»
tasks.hint: When reading from the channel, skip events where (conn == your own number && it is typing). To tell them apart, keep a flag in the event: (conn, kind, json).

tasks.title: Database first, then broadcast
tasks.statement:
Write post(&PgPool, &broadcast::Sender<Event>, user, text) -> Result<i64, sqlx::Error>: it inserts a message (table messages(id BIGSERIAL, author TEXT, text TEXT CHECK (length(text) > 0))) with RETURNING id and ONLY AFTER a successful insert sends Event { id, user, text } into the channel. If the insert fails (an empty text violates the CHECK), nothing goes into the channel. main starts a receiver that, for every event, checks in the database that a row with that id already exists, and prints the result. Publish three messages and one with empty text.

Expected output:
anna: Ok(1)
boris: Ok(2)
anna: Err(Some("23514"))
vera: Ok(4)
[(1, true), (2, true), (4, true)]
tasks.hint: let id = query_scalar(...RETURNING id).fetch_one(pool).await?; let _ = tx.send(...); Ok(id)

tasks.title: The client drops duplicates
tasks.statement:
The client receives events Event { id, text } both over the socket and from catch-up requests, so repeats and different ordering are possible. Write Inbox { seen: BTreeSet<i64> } with a method accept(&mut self, incoming: Vec<Event>) -> Vec<Event>: it returns only new events (the id has not been seen before; repeats inside incoming itself are dropped too, keeping the first occurrence), sorted by id, and remembers them. The method last_id(&self) -> Option<i64> is the largest id seen.

Expected output:
None
[Event { id: 1, text: "a" }, Event { id: 2, text: "b" }, Event { id: 3, text: "c" }]
[Event { id: 4, text: "d" }]
[]
[]
Some(4)
tasks.hint: BTreeSet::insert returns true for a new value; sort the result by id.

tasks.title: Reconnecting and catching up
tasks.hint: Order of checks: the None case, then gap > 200, then After.

tasks.title: A LISTEN/NOTIFY bridge into the hub
tasks.statement:
Several server instances pass events through the database. Write bridge(pool: PgPool, hub: broadcast::Sender<String>), a task that listens on the channel «chat» (PgListener) and publishes every NOTIFY payload into the local broadcast. main starts bridge, subscribes to the hub, sends two NOTIFYs via SELECT pg_notify('chat', $1) from the pool (imitating another instance) and prints what arrived in the hub. First make sure the channel subscription is already in place, and only then send (in main this is done with a short pause).

Expected output:
Ok(Ok("first from another server"))
Ok(Ok("second"))
tasks.hint: PgListener::connect_with(&pool).await?; listener.listen("chat"); loop { let n = listener.recv().await?; let _ = hub.send(n.payload().to_string()); }

tasks.title: Limiting the message size
tasks.statement:
GET /ws: an echo server (replies «echo: TEXT»), but the size of an incoming message is limited to 64 bytes; configure this on WebSocketUpgrade (max_message_size). The client sends a short message (and gets a reply), then one that is too long (200 characters): the server must close the connection, and the next read returns None.

Expected output:
Some("echo: briefly")
None
tasks.hint: upgrade.max_message_size(64).on_upgrade(handle).

tasks.title: Limiting messages per connection
tasks.statement:
Implement ConnLimiter { max: usize, window_ms: u64 } with a method check(&mut self, now_ms: u64) -> Verdict. In a sliding window of window_ms (moments strictly newer than now − window_ms count), at most max messages are allowed: Verdict::Ok means allowed (the moment is remembered); Verdict::Slow(wait_ms) means exceeded, wait wait_ms (until the oldest one leaves the window), and the message is not counted; if 3 messages in a row are rejected within the window, Verdict::Disconnect (after that, every call returns Disconnect too). The count of consecutive rejections is reset by a successful message.

Expected output:
0: Ok
100: Ok
200: Slow(800)
300: Slow(700)
1000: Ok
1100: Ok
1150: Slow(850)
1160: Slow(840)
1170: Disconnect
1180: Disconnect
5000: Disconnect
0: Ok
10: Slow(90)
20: Slow(80)
150: Ok
160: Slow(90)
170: Slow(80)
180: Disconnect
tasks.hint: A Vec<u64> of moments, a strikes counter; retain by window.

tasks.title: Clean closing on shutdown
tasks.statement:
The state is a watch::Receiver<bool> (the shutdown flag). GET /ws: a select! loop between socket.recv() and shutdown.changed(); on shutdown the server sends a Close frame with code 1001 ("going away") and the reason «server is stopping» and ends the handler. main connects a client, waits 100 ms, sets the shutdown flag and prints the Close frame it received: the code and the reason.

Expected output:
«code 1001, reason «server is stopping»»
tasks.hint: Message::Close(Some(CloseFrame { code: 1001, reason: "..".into() })); client: CMsg::Close(Some(frame)), u16::from(frame.code).
